protocol: Autonomy rule: no manual input, but every irregularity is flagged here for human review with the evidence needed to settle it.

irregularities.title: Propensity scale is not identifiable from PU data, and no reachable public index of exhaustively mapped quadrangles exists
irregularities.finding: arXiv:1809.03207 Section 2/5.1 shows the propensity scale cannot be recovered from PU data alone: the likelihood is invariant to a scale transform, so the mean propensity over labelled positives a_bar = E[e(x)|s=1] must be fixed externally. The brief says to anchor it with exhaustively mapped quadrangles if a public index exists. No such index was reachable from this sandbox (nbmg.unr.edu, gbcge.org, usgs.gov, gdr.openei.org and buffedlizard55-lab.github.io are all off the egress allowlist), and the reachable peer-reviewed literature gives only an area share, not a pixel-level index.
irregularities.evidence: Measured a_bar sensitivity of pooled SAR DTI: 0.15 -> 0.06419, 0.25 -> 0.06183, 0.32 -> 0.06116, 0.50 -> 0.05574 (evidence/holdout_pu.json). The ranking is monotone in a_bar but NO anchor makes the SAR arm beat the nnPU baseline, so the gate conclusion is robust to this unidentified nuisance parameter. Also measured: lidar covers 0.7537 of the footprint while Faulds 2026 states detailed maps cover <25% of the region, so lidar coverage is NOT a valid mapping-completeness proxy and was not used as one.
irregularities.disposition: Reported as a sensitivity analysis over a_bar in {0.15, 0.25, 0.32, 0.50}; a_bar=0.25 pre-registered from the peer-reviewed ~25% detailed-mapping figure (Giddens & Faulds 2025, SGP-TR-229). No propensity value is ever quoted as an absolute probability on any deliverable page.
irregularities.to_settle: Obtain the Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology quadrangle map-scale index (free, official, https://nbmg.unr.edu/library/mapinfo.html and the MapInfo GIS metadata release) or the USGS National Geologic Map Database scale inventory, and re-run scripts/02_run_holdout.py --a-bar <anchored value>.

irregularities.title: Template holdout eligibility dilation did not reach the withheld truth (shared-tool bug, fixed in the template pattern)
irregularities.finding: The blocked-holdout cell constructor dilated the VISIBLE labels to build the eligible region. The withheld truth was outside the dilated visible set in most cells, so pooled DTI collapsed to ~0.0008 with no exception raised - a silent, non-crashing instrument failure that would have made every arm look useless and could have killed the lane on a false negative.
irregularities.evidence: Regression test tests/test_metric.py::test_holdout_eligibility_reaches_withheld_truth asserts the withheld truth is inside the eligible region of every cell. Fix: src/gems65/holdout.py Cell.visible_full (and truth_full/active_full) so eligibility is computed on full-grid masks rather than bbox-scoped arrays.
irregularities.disposition: Fixed once in the shared module used by every stage (no private fork). After the fix the instrument returns plausible non-degenerate DTI for all arms.
irregularities.to_settle: Nothing outstanding; the upstream template GEMSDOE32 has the same dilation pattern in its own holdout helper and should be checked.

irregularities.title: Duplicate-check Spearman used positional tie-breaking, so every pair of submission rasters looked correlated (rho ~ 0.97)
irregularities.finding: src/gems65/dupcheck.py spearman_subsample ranked values with np.argsort(np.argsort(x)), which breaks ties by ARRAY POSITION. Submission rasters are ~99.3% zeros, so the zero blocks of any two rasters receive nearly identical rank vectors and the reported rank correlation approaches 1 for statistically independent fields. The parallel-run protocol's drift trigger is rho > 0.90, so this bug alone would have declared lane drift on the FIRST build and stopped the lane on a false positive.
irregularities.evidence: Empirical demonstration on two independent binary fields with the same sparsity: buggy ranking rho = 0.9717, fixed ranking rho = 0.0000, scipy.stats.spearmanr rho = 0.0000. First full build reported max_rho = 0.9743 across all 15 registry rasters; after the fix the same corpus reports max surface rho 0.0318 and max 3-px dot overlap 0.0092. Regression test tests/test_dupcheck.py (5 tests) asserts independent fields give rho ~ 0 and that the implementation matches scipy.
irregularities.disposition: Fixed with scipy.stats.rankdata(method='average') in dupcheck.spearman_subsample and in the two local spearman() helpers in scripts/04_live_mirror.py and scripts/05_holdout_calibration.py that copied the same pattern. This is exactly the 'fix shared tool bugs once in the template, never keep a private fork' case.
irregularities.to_settle: Audit GEMSDOE32 and GEMSDOE for the same argsort-argsort idiom; any registry/dupcheck conclusion drawn before this fix is unsafe.

irregularities.title: EM initialisation deviated from the paper and produced a degenerate fixed point
irregularities.finding: pu.fit_sar_em initialised the latent-positive model f with an nnPU risk at pi=0.5. The paper (Bekker & Davis 2018, Section 5.2) specifies initialising with a balanced model that treats the unlabeled examples as negative. With the wrong init the EM loop converged to f ~ 0.5 everywhere: mean predicted latent-positive probability on unlabeled pixels was 0.4946 and the observed-data log-likelihood got monotonically WORSE each iteration (-0.483 -> -0.612 over 8), i.e. the optimiser was moving away from the maximum.
irregularities.evidence: Fixed initialisation is a class-balanced weighted logistic fit on the selection indicator s via fit_soft_target_logistic, which removes the f==0.5-everywhere fixed point of the old init. The degenerate behaviour nevertheless PERSISTS in the re-run: over 8 iterations mean f|s=0 stays at ~0.45 against a Horvitz-Thompson prevalence pi=0.0517 and em_converged=false (evidence/submission_build.json). Bounded blast radius: the SAR arm's Definition-2 weights come from the ANCHORED propensity e, which is well behaved (range [0.0111,0.4521], coefficients relief +0.63 / slope +0.24 / basin_fill +0.27 / dist_range_front -0.196, i.e. higher selection probability on steep high-relief basin-margin terrain, matching the documented bias direction; 2.2% of weights clipped at 10), so the gate comparison does not depend on f's convergence. The 'em' arm does depend on f and is labelled reference-only for that reason.
irregularities.disposition: Init fixed in src/gems65/pu.py; the related NaN log-likelihood bug (np.clip(f,1e-12,1.0) -> log1p(-1)=-inf -> 0*-inf=NaN, so convergence could never trigger) is also fixed. IR stays OPEN: the EM has not been made to converge, so no EM-derived belief number in this repo is presented as a maximum-likelihood estimate.
irregularities.to_settle: Impose the a_bar anchor INSIDE the EM loop (re-scale e at each M-step so mean e|s=1 == a_bar) and assert the observed-data log-likelihood is non-decreasing, then re-run stages 02 and 03 (~15 min).

irregularities.title: Two conflicting 'highest leaderboard score' values in the standing brief, neither verifiable from this sandbox
irregularities.finding: The brief states in one place that the highest leaderboard score is 0.3774 and elsewhere that 0.3195 is the current highest. The last readable official snapshot (2026-10-04, stored in the sibling template's registry/leaderboard_history.jsonl) shows #1 nchuzhoy 0.3262, #2 kinghorton42 0.3222, #3 DARD 0.3195. So 0.3195 matches a real entry at rank 3 as of that snapshot, and 0.3774 matches nothing on it.
irregularities.evidence: drivendata.org is not on this sandbox's egress allowlist, so the live board cannot be read here. The 0.3774 figure could be a later snapshot taken after 2026-10-04, a final-round score (the scoring mask and label set differ between rounds per forum thread 11516), or a transcription of a different metric.
irregularities.disposition: Both values are recorded; neither is used as a target. All promotion arithmetic in this repo is expressed relative to the registry's own owner-reported scores (0.2376-0.2778) and to the 2026-10-04 snapshot, and every such number is labelled OWNER-REPORT, never ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED.
irregularities.to_settle: Open https://www.drivendata.org/competitions/306/competition-doe-gems/leaderboard/ while signed in and paste the top-5 rows plus the round label into registry/leaderboard_snapshot.jsonl. That converts one number in this repo to ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED.

irregularities.title: The catalogue-hidden holdout structurally cannot reward the lane's own thesis
irregularities.finding: The lane's mechanism is that the catalogue under-represents faults in LOW-propensity terrain, so a SAR model should reallocate belief there. The blocked-holdout proxy's 'truth' is the withheld part of the SAME catalogue, and that withheld truth concentrates in HIGH-propensity terrain. A model that correctly reallocates toward low-propensity terrain is therefore penalised by this instrument by construction. This is a measurement-validity problem, not a bug, and it means the gate result is evidence about the proxy, not conclusive evidence about the live metric.
irregularities.evidence: Measured: pooled DTI SAR 0.06183 vs nnPU 0.06687, delta -0.00504, 95% CI [-0.01015, -0.00111], 2/8 cell wins. The deficit is concentrated exactly where the mechanism predicts: the top-propensity tercile shows SAR 0.06383 vs nnPU 0.07490 (delta -0.01107), i.e. SAR gives up more in high-e terrain than it gains in low-e terrain against catalogue-derived truth. Independently, the template's own prior audit found the catalogue-hidden holdout DRIFTS from live truth (+0.0100 holdout vs -0.0033 live-anchored for the same ranking change), so holdout numbers are proxies only. ADDITIONAL, STRONGER EVIDENCE (stage 05, n=10 registry rasters with owner-reported live scores): Spearman(blocked-holdout pooled DTI, live score) = -0.436 and Spearman(dot count, live) = -0.791. The instrument is ANTI-correlated with the only live evidence available, and the mechanism is now identified: live scoring masks known-fault pixels (forum thread 11516) while this holdout's truth IS catalogue pixels, so catalog-adjacent artifacts (e.g. live 0.2376 -> holdout 0.00000; live 0.2778 -> holdout 0.00452) score near zero on the holdout and the off-catalogue artifacts (holdout 0.0967-0.0997) carry no live score at all. Consequence: the pre-registered gate is respected (not passed -> negative result, no promotion) but it is NOT evidence that the SAR mechanism fails live.
irregularities.disposition: Gate respected as pre-registered: not passed, so the lane is logged NEGATIVE and no file is cleared for submission. Reported together with the measured anti-correlation of the instrument, so the negative result is not over-claimed: it is a negative result ABOUT THE PROXY. The registry-anchored mirror (scripts/04_live_mirror.py) is published as the second, differently-biased view.
irregularities.to_settle: The only clean resolution is one ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED receipt: submit a single SAR-armed file into a weekly slot and read back the score. That is explicitly out of scope here (submission selection is a separate step).

irregularities.title: Data are restored from an owner-supplied GitHub mirror, not from DrivenData
irregularities.finding: The competition data are login-walled and drivendata.org is unreachable from this sandbox, so training_features.tif, labels.tif and sample_submission.tif were restored from GitHub blob mirrors and verified against sha256 pins. The pins are self-consistent across three sibling repos but none of them is organizer-authenticated.
irregularities.evidence: registry/data_manifest.json records sha256, byte length and pin status for all six restored files; scripts/00_restore_data.py re-verifies every hash before any stage is allowed to read the bytes. Grid geometry re-derived independently from the restored files matches the official spec exactly (EPSG:32611, 3730x3292, transform (100,0,243350,0,-100,4508550), footprint 5,167,373 px, catalogue 60,988 px).
irregularities.disposition: Provenance is labelled on every page of the site as owner-supplied and integrity-pinned. If a hash ever fails, stage 00 exits non-zero and the pipeline refuses to run.
irregularities.to_settle: Re-download from the official data page with competition credentials and compare sha256 against registry/data_manifest.json.

irregularities.title: EM convergence diagnostic was mislabelled: the logged 'll' was only the f-part of the complete-data likelihood
irregularities.finding: src/gems65/pu.py fit_sar_em logged sum_i w_i [yhat_i log f_i + (1-yhat_i) log(1-f_i)] as the EM log-likelihood and used its change as the convergence criterion. That quantity is only the f-part of the expected complete-data log-likelihood; monotonicity of a PARTIAL quantity is not an EM guarantee. So the observed monotone decrease (-0.6521 -> -0.6659 over 8 iterations, decrements shrinking to ~0.0012) neither proves nor disproves convergence, and the convergence test built on it was uninformative in both directions.
irregularities.evidence: The SAR observed-data likelihood is sum_i w_i [ s_i log(f_i e_i) + (1-s_i) log(1 - f_i e_i) ]; this is the quantity EM must not decrease. Both are now recorded per iteration as ll_observed and ll_f_surrogate (em_history in evidence/submission_build.json from the next run onward).
irregularities.disposition: Fixed in the shared module src/gems65/pu.py (no fork). The already-published artifacts predate the fix, so their em_history 'll' column must be read as ll_f_surrogate. IR-65-004 stays open until ll_observed is shown non-decreasing on a real run.
irregularities.to_settle: Re-run stage 02/03 after the IR-65-004 anchor-inside-the-loop fix and inspect ll_observed.
